sources.citation: Smith, Alexander D. (comp.); lexibank (eds.). CLDF dataset 'Languages of Borneo' (lexibank/smithborneo), derived from Smith, Alexander D. 2017, The Languages of Borneo: A comprehensive classification, PhD diss., University of Hawai'i at Manoa; dataset source key Smith, A. D. & T. Rama 2022, 'Environmental factors affect the evolution of linguistic subgroups in Borneo', Diachronica 39(2): 193-225, doi:10.1075/dia.20024.smi. Doculect 'Beketan' = buki1248/bkn, 674 forms.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing: 674 Beketan forms in IPA with segmentations (e.g. melaʔ 'false', kəbalum 'after', pəʤaʤaw 'always', baɭum 'already'); the stress sign occurs 0 times in the Beketan rows and 0 times in the whole 50,997-lexeme dataset; no comments, no orthography note. Usable for syllable-shape statistics (many disyllables with schwa penults) but carries no stress or tone information.

sources.citation: Smith, Alexander D. 2017. The Languages of Borneo: A comprehensive classification. PhD diss., University of Hawai'i at Manoa. 723 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: First-hand Bekatan data (consultant Elin Ester, Kampung Tubol, Belayan R., East Kalimantan, p. 11) in sec. 2.4 'Punan' (printed pp. 111-127: sound correspondences, six-vowel system, no off-glides). The word 'stress' never occurs in the Punan section; stress is discussed only for Merap, Segai-Modang, Hliboi Bidayuh and W. Kalimantan Malayic. Silent on Bukitan/Bekatan stress.

sources.citation: Chan, Henry. 2007. Survival in the Rainforest: Change and Resilience among the Punan Vuhang of Eastern Sarawak, Malaysia. PhD dissertation, University of Helsinki (Research Series in Anthropology). ISBN 978-952-10-3919-5. hdl:10138/23463.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No phonology content: an anthropological dissertation (21 months fieldwork 1993-95) with a Punan Vuhang-English glossary (Appendix 1, pp. 345ff, plain roman spelling, no stress or length marks), song texts with translations, a passage on Harrisson's whistle language and two-syllable personal 'jungle call' names (quoting Harrisson 1965 on their 'tone'), and a note on linguistic affinity (Ukit, Sihan, Punan Bah). Searched stress/accent/tone/pitch/syllable/penult/orthograph/pronunc/phonolog/vowel: no statement about word stress or lexical tone. Bibliography identifies Wilson, E. Bryant 1972 'A s…
